prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using heterobifunctional small molecules that recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate proteins

statement.case_for: In my opening ballot I ranked Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (B043) first on pure synthetic-chemistry merit, but the opening ballots show that targeted protein degradation (B029) is the one candidate that nearly every member placed in the top three (seven of eight), and on reflection it is where my own criteria also lead. It is a new chemical concept: a small molecule is designed as a bifunctional adaptor that induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a target, turning degradation into a catalytic, event-driven pharmacology. The chemistry is designable and tunable (linker, ligase ligand, ternary-complex cooperativity), the mechanism has been confirmed by many independent groups, and the pipeline is large. The PROTAC concept (Crews and Deshaies, 2001) and the VHL-ligand and structural work that made it rational (Ciulli) give a coherent heterobifunctional-degrader story that fits within three names.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is yet approved, so clinical vindication is incomplete and the award could be seen as early. A prize built on Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli leaves out the cereblon and molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray and others), and also Sakamoto, who co-authored the 2001 paper. The citation must therefore be worded narrowly around heterobifunctional degraders, and some members will see that as an arbitrary cut. B043 is more mature and its attribution is cleaner, but a second palladium cross-coupling prize after 2010 is a real objection that I cannot dismiss.

responses.point: Aili ranks B029 first and would credit Crews, Deshaies and Handa, so that the prize covers both PROTACs and cereblon-based molecular glues.
responses.response: I understand the wish to capture the glue strand, but I do not think Handa belongs beside Crews and Deshaies in one citation. Cereblon identification is a target-identification discovery that explains thalidomide, whereas PROTACs are a designed modality. Combining them makes the citation vague. I would rather credit the designed-degrader invention cleanly and accept that the glue strand is left out, unless the committee wants a two-part prize, which the three-person limit makes impractical here.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks Gray and Winkler's long-range protein electron transfer first and ranks B029 second with Crews, Ciulli and Handa, while noting that any three-name split leaves real credit disputes.
responses.response: I agree with Brzezinski that the credit dispute is real, but I would place Deshaies ahead of Handa: the 2001 PROTAC paper is the founding demonstration, and Handa's work belongs to a different mechanistic line. On B056, I respect the mechanistic rigour, and it is a clean pair, but electron transfer through proteins has a smaller reach beyond biophysical chemistry and, with Marcus already recognised in 1992, I see it as a worthy but second-tier option.

responses.point: Linke ranks halide perovskites (B058) first, stressing the speed with which efficiency rose and the clear defect-tolerance physics, while conceding that stability and scale-up are open.
responses.response: I accept that perovskites are a major development and I kept B058 in my top three. Still, I weigh the chemical-invention content differently. Much of the perovskite story is materials and device physics, the credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis is very crowded, and Kojima falls outside the credited list. With stability and lead toxicity unresolved, I find the maturity argument weaker than for B029, so I keep it as an alternative and not the preferred choice.

responses.point: Zou ranks base editing (B047) first and photoredox catalysis (B033) second, and notes that MacMillan already holds a 2021 prize and credit in photoredox is spread across many groups.
responses.response: I agree with Zou's own caveat about photoredox: with MacMillan already a laureate and the credit divided among seven or more groups, there is no clean three-person prize, and I ranked it only seventh. For base editing, I see the chemical invention clearly, but the CRISPR prize of 2020 and the unresolved Kondo/Nishida question make it harder to frame than B029, and its clinical record is younger.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B029 first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, and sees the recognition as timely despite few approved drugs.
responses.response: I largely share this and use the same trio. I would add that 'timely' depends on how heavily the committee weights approval. The mechanism is validated in many independent laboratories, so I would not wait for a drug approval, but I would insist that the citation stay on the heterobifunctional design principle.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a prize that excludes the cereblon/molecular-glue strand and Sakamoto, or insists on a broader citation.
Whether the lack of an approved degrader drug makes B029 premature relative to mature candidates such as B043.
Whether a second Pd cross-coupling prize after 2010 is acceptable for B043, and whether Kosugi/Migita precedent affects its attribution; my account of the early history is from memory.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I share a Lund affiliation with Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr and trained under Masamune, but none of the shortlisted candidates is a colleague, student or collaborator that my profile documents. Hartwig is unconnected to me on the record available.
